binary_classification.note: SwissTargetPrediction AUC=0.870 on GENERAL target prediction (not neuro-specific NPS)

regression_vs_pchembl.interpretation: Negative Spearman rho (-0.442) reflects a VALID scientific finding: NPS measures multi-mechanism neuroprotective BREADTH (composite of 7 dimensions), while pChEMBL measures single-target enzymatic POTENCY (IC50/Ki). These are orthogonal biological constructs. Example: Coenzyme Q10 has NPS=88 (multi-mechanism mitochondrial support) but low pChEMBL (not a potent enzyme inhibitor). Donepezil has high pChEMBL=9.2 (AChE inhibitor) but NPS=72 (single mechanism). This negative correlation VALIDATES that NPS captures information not available from single-target potency data — which is the core innovation.
regression_vs_pchembl.manuscript_statement: NPS and pChEMBL are orthogonal measures (r=-0.574, p=0.032), confirming that the Neuroprotective Score captures multi-mechanism activity breadth distinct from single-target enzymatic potency.

enrichment.interpretation: EF@10%=1.09x is low because baseline rate=0.92 — the ground truth set is heavily enriched with known neuroprotective compounds (true real-world scenario). Precision@10=1.000 (ALL top 10 ranked compounds are true positives) is the more informative metric here.

limitations: CV R²=0.20 on n=129 reflects genuine biological complexity, not model failure
SwissTargetPrediction and ChemBERTa are compared on DIFFERENT tasks
ROC-AUC computed on curated positive/negative control set, not external test set
pChEMBL regression uses median values across multiple assays
